gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that mere C1 regularity does not guarantee complete characteristic flow existence for all required times, so the characteristic-based domains and dependent results are undefined or unsupported; both give a global-existence or growth-condition repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The stated regularity assumptions do not ensure global-in-time characteristic existence and bounded-domain flow constructions for arbitrary time pairs.

component_coverage.gold_component: Failure of the old C1 assumptions to guarantee complete characteristics, with consequent ill-defined evolved domains and dependent results.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly supplies finite-time blow-up under C1 regularity, explains the resulting failure of CODE and evolved-domain constructions and arbitrary-time theorems, and proposes global existence or linear growth.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false unit-Jacobian/change-of-variables step in the characteristic flow for general compressible velocity fields, including the resulting Lp scaling and the need to propagate Jacobian factors through downstream estimates.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The characteristic flow is not generally measure preserving: its Jacobian is determined by the velocity divergence, so exact Lp norm invariance is false without a divergence-free assumption.

component_coverage.gold_component: False exact Lp norm invariance caused by omission of the flow Jacobian, affecting both whole-space and moving-domain lemmas and downstream estimates.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 directly identifies the flow-map derivative error, gives the divergence/Jacobian formula and counterexample, traces the false norm identities into the boundedness and stability arguments, and supplies Jacobian-weighted repairs.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 discusses an incorrect Jacobian and resulting norm estimates in the boundedness argument, but it never identifies the separate domain-of-definition failure caused by evaluating an arbitrary W in H(G) outside G or supplies the required zero extension.

ISSUE-002 concerns an invalid proof manipulation involving support points and nonvanishing values for a transported function. It does not diagnose the distinct inference that equality of an element function's support with the domain fails to establish compact containment and hence membership in the paper's H0 space.
